question: Does native iTunes 12.13.11.1 open, use and persist a library file whose track metadata was rewritten by itlkit rather than by iTunes?

planned_edit.value: ITL research EXP-01 written by itlkit

protocol: compare raw bytes and COM at every step
acceptance_requires_all_of: iTunes opens the intended file, not a rebuilt or fallback library
no damaged-file dialog and no unexpected modal
no 'iTunes Library (Damaged).itl' and no change in the library file count
COM reports the value itlkit wrote
a normal COM Quit, not a kill
the value is still present after restart 1 and restart 2
itlkit can still read the file iTunes leaves behind
does_not_count_as_acceptance: byte identity of the file iTunes rewrites
failure_signals: edited value reverts after a restart
playback: not tested, reported separately from acceptance

amendment_1.reason: the declared metadata edit is refused by itlkit itself
amendment_1.observed_refusal: UnsupportedError: writes require the observed Windows iTunes 12.13.9.1/12.13.10.3 profile
amendment_1.interpretation: the semantic write path is version gated, and the only native library available here was written by 12.13.11.1, a build whose record profile itlkit has not observed. This is a finding, not a workaround opportunity: the guard is doing exactly what it was built to do.
amendment_1.revised_subject: a container level reconstruction produced by itlkit, which carries the same logical library but is not a file iTunes has ever written
amendment_1.unchanged: every acceptance criterion and every non-acceptance rule from the original declaration still applies
